'''Vladimir Grigorevich Boltyansky''' ({{langx|ru|Влади́мир Григо́рьевич Болтя́нский}}; 26 April 1925 – 16 April 2019),<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://math.ru/history/people/boltyanskiy |title=Болтянский Владимир Григорьевич |lang=ru |website=math.ru |access-date=2019-04-19}}</ref> also transliterated as '''Boltyanski''', '''Boltyanskii''', or '''Boltjansky''', was a [[USSR|Soviet]] and [[Russia]]n [[mathematician]], [[educator]] and author of popular mathematical books and articles.  He was best known for his books on [[topology]], [[combinatorial geometry]] and [[Hilbert's third problem]].

== Biography ==
Boltyansky was born in [[Moscow]].<ref>[http://www.ega-math.narod.ru/LSP/book.htm Lev Pontryagin's memoirs], p. 214.</ref> He served in the [[Soviet army]] during [[World War II]], when he was a [[signaller]] on the [[2nd Belorussian Front]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://may9.ru/en/section.php?docId=10624 |title=60 Anniversary World War II Celebrations |access-date=11 August 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070811140549/http://may9.ru/en/section.php?docId=10624 |archive-date=11 August 2007 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref> He graduated from [[Moscow University]] in 1948, where his advisor was [[Lev Pontryagin]].  He defended his "[[Doktor nauk]] in physics and mathematics" ([[higher doctorate]]) degree in 1955, became a professor in 1959.

Boltyansky was awarded the [[Lenin Prize]] (for the work led by Pontryagin, [[Revaz Gamkrelidze]], and {{Interlanguage link multi|Evgenii Mishchenko|ru|3=Мищенко, Евгений Фролович}}) for applications of [[differential equations]] to [[optimal control]], where he was one of the discoverers of the [[Pontryagin's maximum principle]].<ref>L.S. Pontryagin, V.G. Boltyanskii, R.V. Gamkredilze, and E.F. Mishenko. [https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/zamm.19630431023 The mathematical theory of optimal processes.] Interscience Publishers, John Wiley & Sons Inc., New York - London, 1962.</ref> In 1967 he received [[Uzbek Soviet Socialist Republic|Uzbek SSR]] prize for the work on [[ordered ring]]s.  He taught at [[CIMAT]].<ref>[http://www.cimat.mx/es/node/643 Faculty profile] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201113020/http://www.cimat.mx/es/node/643 |date=1 February 2014 }}, CIMAT, Retrieved 2014-01-19.</ref>

He was the corresponding member of the [[Russian Academy of Education]]. He was the author of over 200 books and mathematical articles.
